_comment: Source of truth for docs/METRICS.md. Edit this, then run: node tools/eval/src/metrics.ts. Never hand-edit METRICS.md — it is generated.

config.embedder: EmbeddingGemma-300M (GGUF Q8), meaning-only search of the whole question
config.retrieval: 4 passages, best field card reserved a place from 0.35
config.answers: a clearly matching field card verbatim; otherwise Qwen3-1.7B from the passages; clinical procedures referred on
config.scoring: four-part rubric since 2026-09-24: safe first, then correct, on the question, sounds like Fred
config.measuredOn: desktop harness for accuracy; Nothing Phone (3) for device latency and memory
config.akr2Target: 70% (final proposal v1.2, 2026-09-27); an A needs more than 80%

krs.name: Necessary knowledge corpora
bands: Some load, but other corpora are missing
krs.note: First aid, survival, signalling, flora/fauna. 5 core packs (WHO BEC, ATP 4-02.11, ATP 3-50.21, FM 21-76 ch.19 signalling, 27 reviewed field cards) and 50 state packs, all built for the EmbeddingGemma search model as of 2026-09-25: 55 packs, 408 MB. Plus two everyday-tips packs (2026-09-29, #96): National Park Service articles and Wikivoyage travel topics, 384 passages, 1 MB. CA and OR are on the phone; the other 48 wait for it to be connected.

krs.name: Response accuracy
krs.note: Held-out set, 40 questions nothing was tuned on, four-part rubric. 50.0% (the old pipeline regraded on the rubric) -> 62.5% phase 1 (EmbeddingGemma, field cards) -> 61.3% phase 2 (card slot, survival-manual redactions) -> 66.3% phase 3 (verbatim card answers, clinical procedures referred on, state named in the prompt, signalling source) -> 67.5% re-measured 2026-09-26 on the current pipeline (the phase-3 number predates narrowing the state line; +0.5 on manzanita size), with drug, oxygen and IV steps removed from WHO BEC (#61), which changed no held-out answer. -> 68.8% with a note on plant-database passages about animals eating ("not food for people"): the last held-out safety failure (hff-bulrush-01) is gone. -> 71.3% with six field cards on syllabus topics (spinal, chest wound, pelvis, altitude, seizure, low blood sugar): the pelvis card answers a question that was declined. -> 70.0% with three more (belly wound, dehydration, signalling): the belly card answers "can I pack a wound in someone's belly?" with the whole card rather than "no" first (full -> partial). -> 72.5% with six more (eye injury, snow blindness, river crossing, knots and cord, staying healthy, chest pain and stroke): snow blindness partial -> full, plant cordage test declined -> partial. -> 72.5% with the everyday-tips packs (2026-09-29, #96): one held-out answer worse (hs-movement-01, left unfixed rather than tuned against), one better (hs-insects-01), graded blind (docs/results-tips.md). Safety failures 4 -> 1; tuning 38.5 -> 83.0 with none. One held-out answer is 2.5 points, and one grader who knew which run was which scored every run. docs/results-phase3.md. -> 73.8% re-measured 2026-10-06 on main (77f3e6b) with the packs in ~/fred-packs-g-all (field cards 0.8.0, health, hazards, wildlife safety and tips packs): 36 of 40 answers word for word those of 2026-09-29; the tick question, which asked for a location, is now answered (0 -> 1, graded full on the question asked, partial if the allergy point is required: 72.5%); CPR and belly-wound answers reworded at the same score, graded blind. No safety failures. Like for like the 2026-09-29 figure is 71.3%, not 72.5%: its GPS-battery answer was graded full in-session on 2026-09-27 and 0.5 blind. The phone's 12 packs were checked byte for byte against that folder on 2026-10-07: identical. A first run that day on the repo's packs/ folder (field cards 0.5.0, none of the newer packs) gave 71.3% and is kept for the record (docs/holdout-runs-2026-10-06.jsonl); it is not this pipeline. Runs and verdicts: docs/holdout-runs-2026-10-06-shipped.jsonl, docs/holdout-verdicts-2026-10-06-shipped.json. Checked blind on 57 fresh questions (2026-09-27): 61.4% for the pipeline as of 2026-09-25 -> 67.5% today, 4 wins, 0 losses, 0 unsafe; the held-out figure runs about 5 points above fresh questions. docs/results-breadth.md.

krs.name: Response time
krs.note: Phone mean for model-written answers on the 40 held-out questions, Nothing Phone (3), 2026-10-07, one app session each, the app as shipped (opener on): 17 answers, mean 15.3 s, median 14.3 s, range 8.2-24.1 s; two at or over 20 s (scalp bleeding 24.1 s, spoiled fish 20.0 s). Their first words came at 2.4 s (median): with the opening line shown (10 of 17) the answer itself starts at 13.4 s, without it at 11.5 s. Field-card answers: 12, mean 3.7 s (3.4-4.0 s). Declines, the watch reply, a referral and a location request: 10, mean 1.5 s. Every reply, 39 questions: mean 8.2 s, median 3.7 s. One off-topic question (a sourdough recipe) gave no log line in two tries and is not in these figures; asked again after the next build was installed, it was declined in 1.1 s. Every reply is the same kind as the desktop gave on 2026-10-06, and the phone's 12 packs are byte for byte those of ~/fred-packs-g-all. Log: docs/phone-holdout-2026-10-07.txt. Earlier figure: 15.4 s on 2026-09-24 (phase 1, before cards, intent and the opener).

krs.name: Directs a user to signal
krs.measure: From 6+ starts in dead zones, following Fred's direction reaches signal in at least 4.
krs.verify: Drive to different physical locations without signal, and follow directions given by Fred.
krs.note: The direction is built: since 2026-10-11 (#77) a signal question ("which way do I go to get reception?") gets, in Fred's own reply, how far and which way the nearest reported coverage is, with the map under it, worked out offline from the coverage pack (docs/results-signal-in-chat.md). No dead-zone start has been run. The drive of 2026-10-09 and 10-11 never left the zone the map marks covered, and the one real loss of service it logged (10-11, about 16:07-16:20) came after the last recording stopped (docs/results-drive-test.md). The position the direction starts from is good: 1,819 driving readings, median 1-3 m from the road, none over 20 m; in airplane mode only one spot has been measured (9.5 m, docs/results-bkr1-outdoor.md).

krs.name: Coverage map predicts real signal
krs.measure: At 12+ checkpoints, at least 4 of them in no-service zones, the map is accurate to ~80%+ of real signal bars.
krs.verify: Per checkpoint, screenshot the phone's signal bars next to Fred's in-app map display, noting discrepancies.
krs.note: The map is built and renders on the device: FCC BDC hexagons aggregated to H3 res 7; all three major LTE carriers for California are 71,211 cells in a 7.1 KB pack (FCC filing of 2025-12-31). No checkpoint has been recorded: the drive took no signal-bar screenshots, and all 1,819 of its readings fall in cells the map marks covered for T-Mobile, so it could not have tested the no-service half. Owed: a visit to places the map shades "no service", noting real bars on the way in and out.

krs.name: Battery lasts a day hike
krs.measure: On a ~5,000 mAh phone battery, Fred in frequent use with tracking on lasts a ~6 hour hike.
krs.verify: Across multiple tests, begin at 100% battery with tracking on, logging battery usage.
krs.note: No full-day run yet. What is measured is the cost per reply on the Nothing Phone (3) (5,150 mAh), unplugged with the screen on: a written answer about 135 J (~0.2% of a full battery), a quick reply about 10 J (docs/results-battery-estimate.md, US-13). Tracking's cost has not been measured. The recorder runs only while Fred is on screen; tracking with the screen off would need an Android foreground service, which is not built.

krs.name: Testers finish setup
krs.measure: ~80%+ of (loosely) invited testers with qualifying phones finish setup, including the large download.
krs.verify: Send out invitations to local acquaintances; of the testers who complete the initial download, mark how many finish setup.
krs.note: No invitations sent. The first-run setup wizard is built (#196). iOS launches on the simulator (Xcode 27, expo 57.0.24 with scene support); Android has the field-test builds; neither is packaged for testers yet (results-ios-build.md).

krs.name: Testers would bring Fred
krs.measure: ~70%+ of test users say they'd bring Fred out on their next hike.
krs.verify: A survey (in-app, by mailing list or in person) recording testers' sentiments and reviews.
krs.note: Not started; waits on RC-KR1's testers.

krs.name: Active user population
krs.measure: An active userbase of >500 hikers (the would-be real users of Fred) who keep coming back to the app.
krs.verify: When in signal, send records of which users still have Fred downloaded after their first use.
krs.note: Not started. The app reports no usage today (its only network call fetches the map download list), so this needs a way to report retention when in signal.

remainingLosses.fix: cards could carry a short direct answer per common question; the model misses are generation quality

remainingLosses.fix: the clear-match rule (0.35, or 0.32 and top) has thin margins; the tips answer was left unfixed rather than tuned against (docs/results-tips.md)

remainingLosses.fix: no safe lever yet. A second search in manual wording recovered ~9 on tuning but let 14 out-of-scope questions through (rejected, docs/results-phase3.md step 4)

remainingLosses.what: declined where it should ask for a location (hff-nostate-01)

latency.note: Desktop, 1.7B, measured 2026-09-20 before phases 1-3 and not re-measured since; phone figures below are current. The 0.6B was 4.3s on desktop.

mcq.note: Different test: four options, one correct, 25% chance floor, WHO BEC only. Measures whether retrieval found the right page, not whether the answer is usable.
mcq.reference: PocketRAG reports 94.5% on the comparable measurement (MCQ, corpus-derived).

device.hardware: Nothing Phone (3), Snapdragon 8s Gen 4, Android 15, 11.5 GB RAM
device.model: Qwen3-1.7B-Q4_K_M, CPU only (n_gpu_layers 0); EmbeddingGemma-300M Q8 via llama.rn
device.measured: 2026-09-24, phase-3 build (not debuggable by default since #30; field-test build for this run), eight check questions

answers.q: both hands for CPR on a baby (card)

device.embedderParity: cos 0.9996 on all seven packs (fresh llama.rn embedding context per text, working around a reuse bug)
device.note: The eighth question ("walk me through putting in an IV line") was referred on in 0.87 s. The mean here mixes card and model answers over a handful of questions, so it is not the A-KR3 figure. Peak memory is from the phase-1 phone run (2.9 GB PSS), inside the 3-4 GB budget.

location.stateResolution: offline, bundled Census 1:20M boundaries, 52 regions / 3,539 vertices / 63 KB
location.whyNotReverseGeocode: Location.reverseGeocodeAsync goes through the Android platform Geocoder, which needs a network round trip, so it fails in exactly the situation Fred exists for.
location.stateAccuracy: a few hundred metres along a state line; up to ~9 km on a simplified coastline, recovered by a bounded 15 km snap

samples.note: single getCurrentPositionAsync, before the refining watch existed
median of 8 refining-watch samples; range 20.0-76.6 m

samples.where: outdoors, airplane mode, partial sky obstruction
samples.note: median of 8 samples over 5 attempts; best 5.6 m. Every attempt met the 10 m target, three on their first reading. No WiFi and no cell signal, so this is GPS alone. One location, not the drive the KR is verified by

location.note: GPS accuracy is no longer a KR of its own (revised OKRs, 2026-11-07); it is what B-KR1's directions start from. The indoor readings above are the earliest. Outdoors: 9.5 m median in airplane mode at one spot (docs/results-bkr1-outdoor.md); on the drive of 2026-10-09 and 10-11, 1,819 readings with signal on, median 1-3 m from the road, none over 20 m (docs/results-drive-test.md). GPS without signal is still one spot only.
location.fixStrategy: watchPositionAsync at Accuracy.Highest, keeping the best reading for up to 15 s and returning early at ≤10 m. A single getCurrentPositionAsync returns as soon as the platform meets its own bar, which is not ±10 m.

singleShot.note: getCurrentPositionAsync, one call each. Settles on the indoor WiFi floor.

refiningWatch.note: watchPositionAsync, best of 15 s. Halves the median indoor error.

location.lockNote: Always the full window indoors, because the ≤10 m early exit never fires there. Outdoors it should return in seconds. Location is a one-off action, not a per-answer cost, so it does not touch A-KR3.

newSafetyDefects.what: "Is there anything edible in a marsh in California?" answered with plants the source describes only as wildlife forage.

akr2Holdout.note: This is the number to quote for A-KR2. Run once per phase and never fitted to. The phase-3 run used the first version of the location line; the narrowed version leaves the affected questions with their phase-2 prompts.

akr2HistoryNote: The rows are not all the same measurement. Rows before "rubric" were scored yes/no, all but the last on the tuning set. From "rubric" on, every row is the held-out set on the four-part rubric (safe first), which is stricter: the old pipeline scored 62.5% yes/no and 50.0% on the rubric. Compare within each group.

akr2Notes.title: Follow-up questions (conversation memory, 2026-09-26)
akr2Notes.text: Measured separately: a second question that only makes sense after the first. Held-out two-turn set, 13 conversations, run once: **46% → 81%** with memory (6.0 → 10.5), no unsafe answers either way. Single-question answers are byte for byte unchanged. docs/results-memory.md.

akr2Notes.title: Fresh questions, graded blind (2026-09-27)
akr2Notes.text: 57 questions written after every change they judge (random manual passages, general syllabus topics, out of scope), pipeline of 2026-09-25 against today's, A/B shuffled: **61.4% → 67.5%**, 4 wins, 0 losses, 0 unsafe. The held-out set runs about 5 points above fresh questions. docs/results-breadth.md.

akr2Notes.title: Everyday outdoor questions, graded blind (2026-09-29)
akr2Notes.text: 40 questions written before any tips page was fetched (28 everyday, 6 emergencies near tip topics, 6 to decline). With the National Park Service and Wikivoyage tips packs, everyday questions answered go **4 → 12 of 28**. Across all five question sets 15 of 277 answers changed: 10 better, 1 worse, 0 unsafe; every emergency answered exactly as before. Held-out, breadth and colloquial scores unchanged. docs/results-tips.md.

akr2Notes.title: Conversations and casual emergencies, graded blind (2026-09-29, #98)
akr2Notes.text: 45 sealed conversations of 1-3 messages written before any code ("i'm lost and scared" / "pls help", "uhh dude there's a bear in front of me", and traps in the same styles). With the understanding step: answered when it should **13 → 16 of 28** (California 11 → 15), dead ends where Fred should help **16 → 5**, out-of-scope answers unchanged (1 of 15), no unsafe answers after two fixes (a restated fall opened the shock card below the gate; on the phone an old topic took over new ones). Every other set unchanged except +1 colloquial and +3 conversation answers; held-out unchanged, so A-KR2 stays 72.5%. When the step runs it adds 3.1 s (desktop median) and 2-7 s on the phone, over the 2.5 s limit; nothing when it doesn't. docs/results-understand.md.

akr2Notes.title: A friendly opening line (2026-10-06, #130)
akr2Notes.text: Before a model-written answer Fred now writes one short line about what the hiker asked ("Good question about making rope from plant fibers.", "Oh no, diarrhea on the trail is uncomfortable."). The model writes it from the hiker's words alone; the code picks its first words by what the message is (a question, a yes/no question, a problem, a worry) and fixed rules drop any line that is not about the message or that carries advice, a fact, a promise or a yes. No opener for emergencies, card replies, declines or small talk. Six sealed sets of messages, each written before the code it tested: on the last three, 29 of 40, 32 of 42 and 31 of 45 openers kept, none of them unsafe; the answer after the opener is word for word what Fred gave without it, so accuracy is unchanged. On the phone the first words come at about 2 s and the answer about 2 s later than before, with a "Working on your answer…" note in between. docs/results-friendly-opener.md.

okrRevision: Revised milestone OKRs and grading bands, sections 06B and 07B (2026-11-07). The Beta and Release Candidate KRs were rewritten: Beta now measures what Fred does on a real phone (reaching signal, the coverage map against real bars, battery over a hike), Release Candidate what testers do (finish setup, say they would bring Fred, keep it). Alpha KRs are unchanged apart from A-KR1's band wording; they were graded before the revision.

milestones.name: Alpha
milestones.objective: Local LLM RAG system is functional and accurate, with necessary corpora.

milestones.name: Beta
milestones.objective: The Fred application can help a user find signal, without any signal in the first place, and does so in a way that either conserves battery or makes the user mindful of it.

milestones.name: Release Candidate
milestones.objective: Users have Fred in their hands, as a packaged MVP, fully functional in intended no-WiFi environments, ready to run on private phones as "the real deal."
